items.heading: The Daily Reality Varies More
items.text: The Daily Reality Varies More The Daily Reality Varies More The daily reality varies more by track than most outsiders expect. A 2D animator spends the day timing character poses frame by frame or adjusting rigged puppets in Toon Boom. A 3D character animator blocks out poses, refines an arc, and reviews playblasts with a supervisor.

items.heading: Before You Commit Months
items.text: Before you commit months to any course or tutorial series, understand what each track actually asks of you, not just what it pays or how it looks in a reel. The order below is not alphabetical or based on which sounds most prestigious: it leads with the tracks that have the most real growth and growth headroom. Motion graphics leads because it has the lowest gatekeeping and the clearest route to owning a freelance practice or small studio, not just a salary.

items.heading: Structured Pipeline Training That Mirrors
items.text: Structured pipeline training that mirrors how a real studio production works, which matters more in 3D and VFX than in motion graphics.

items.heading: Placement Cells and Studio Tie
items.text: Placement cells and studio tie-ups that give a first foot in the door, especially for the outsourcing-heavy VFX and 3D studios that hire in batches.

items.heading: A Cost and Time Commitment
items.text: A cost and time commitment: diploma and degree programs typically run one to three years and carry real fees, so this only pays off if you finish with a strong reel, not just a certificate.
